title: GOG taken offline for maintenance in wake of PHP security emergency
summary: GOG and GOG Galaxy were taken offline following news of critical web vulnerabilities.
body: The reveal of critical vulnerabilities affecting the PHP scripting language used in web development have led a number of major websites and services to go offline today as a precaution while they apply security fixes. DRM-free game store GOG announced at 8 am Pacific that its site and launcher, GOG Galaxy, would be offline for "a couple of hours" for maintenance. The company did not say the cause, but it is not hard to speculate. We’re temporarily taking GOG offline for maintenance for a couple of hours. GOG GALAXY will also be offline during this time. We apologize for the inconvenience and appreciate your patience! October 21, 2026 Numerous other outages are being reported this morning as security teams scramble to protect their websites and services. The government of Finland took down websites as a precaution, for instance, and (perhaps less importantly) we're hearing from players that Final Fantasy 14 login servers are down.

title: 'You've taken us free cash flow negative as a company, so congratulations': Amazon has plenty of Nvidia GPUs, but not enough energy to power its AI boom
summary: Meanwhile, the RTX 5090 remains missing in action.
body: Nvidia's RTX 5090 GPU is 'unavailable' from many reputable retailers, approaching an asking price of $9,000 if you happen to track one down on Newegg's marketplace of resellers of dubious virtue. The AI boom is at least in part to blame for this, encouraging team green to shift production resources away from consumer hardware. However, business customers like Amazon are running into logistical issues that just add insult to injury for PC gamers left out in the cold. Amazon Web Services took delivery of approximately $5 billion of Nvidia GB300 racks in August alone, according to an email seen by Business Insider . Reportedly, the cloud company has also accepted $3 billion worth of hardware each month since. The kicker is that, despite having all of this kit lined up to install in its data centres, AWS does not yet have enough energy to power everything. This is one reason AWS's free cash flow dropped from $53 billion in Q2 of 2024 , to $7.6 billion during Q2 2026 . title: 'We expect mass attacks to start within 15 minutes of the release': Web admins braced for emergency PHP updates to plug leaked high-severity holes
summary: Batten down the virtual hatches.
body: The PHP security team has given advanced notice of an upcoming fix for two critical security vulnerabilities, both rated at 9.2 out of 10 on the CVE severity scale. Info about the flaws seems to have leaked ahead of their official disclosure, as a video is being shared which reportedly shows a tool called PHP2Shell being used to remotely execute code on webservers via the vulnerabilities (via Ars Technica ). The PHP programming language is widely used across the internet and powers a huge number of websites. The fix is due to be released at 2pm UTC (10 am ET). Researchers from cybersecurity firm Sansec say the vulnerabilities affect all web servers running PHP 5.4 or later, and that "we expect mass attacks to start within 15 minutes of the release." Dane Knecht, the chief technology officer for Cloudflare, says the company is already updating its firewall rules for PHP sites. "We are seeing early attacks emerging and are updating mitigations as new vectors show up. This is a stopgap only," Knecht posted on X . "Patch as soon as @ThePHPF releases the update at 14:00 UTC today." Speaking to Bleeping Computer yesterday, the CEO of cybersecurity firm WatchTowr, Benjamin Harris, said: …

title: Chinese repair centre has received 7 melted 12+4-pin Nvidia GPUs in just the past two days alone
summary: This is not getting better, is it?
body: YouTube channel, 修电脑的张哥 , roughly translated to Zhang the Computer Repairman, has posted a video this morning because of the sheer volume of Nvidia GPUs they have had sent in for repair in just the past two days alone. And they're all because of burnt interfaces between the 12+4-pin power cable and the card itself. Seven cards in total have come in for repair (via Uniko's Hardware ), mostly RTX 5090 cards, along with Asus and MSI RTX 4090. They all come from various manufacturers; as well as Asus and MSI there is also a Gainward card in the mix as well as a Founders Edition RTX 5090 , too. You can see in the video that either the socket interface is burned, sometimes blackening the PCB, or the 12+4-pin power connector itself has melted into the socket and the user has had to snip the cable off in order to be able to send the card in for testing. Zhang makes the necessary repairs to each of the cards—removing the interface, cleaning the contacts, and soldering on a new 12+4-pin socket—and then goes ahead and tests each one of them. With the new sockets in place, the repaired cards are back in action and while the GPUs run through some 3DMark benchmarks he checks the temperatures on…

title: Founder of bankrupt Samson studio mulls how to use AI for his next attempt: 'Cutting corners in game development has a habit of coming back to bite you in the ass'
summary: Christopher Sundberg said the goal for his next studio is to make "a game we can afford to finish without needing every sales forecast to come true."
body: Christofer Sundberg, the founder of Samson developer Liquid Swords, has confirmed the studio's closure, saying that while the console version of the game enjoyed "much greater success" than the PC release, it "wasn't enough to get the company across the finish line." Reports over the weekend revealed that Liquid Swords had gone bankrupt just six months after the PC release of Samson, which was followed by a console launch in September. "It's been a hell of a ride and a lot of fun, even when the circumstances gave us very little to laugh about," Sundberg wrote. "Building a studio, creating Samson and releasing it on PC and consoles took an enormous amount of work from people who cared deeply about what we were making. "The console versions met with much greater success than the PC release. We got them out, but that success wasn't enough to get the company across the finish line. Market conditions and some bad business decisions brought us here, and I own my part in that. I can look honestly at what went wrong and still be proud of what we built." Samson wasn't especially well received when it debuted on PCs, and while post-launch updates have tightened it up, it still holds a very …

title: I have neither the budget nor the inclination for a crystal encrusted RTX 5090, but Galax is releasing one anyway
summary: These stones ain't no friends of mine.
body: Nvidia's RTX 5090 GPU has become particularly elusive lately. In light of swirling rumours, Nvidia promises the 5090 isn't dead but constrained supply and runaway pricing has made it a tough card to track down. So, amidst all of this, what does Palit-owned hardware manufacturer Galax do? Tease a gem-studded edition of the RTX 5090. The GeForce RTX 5090 Hall of Fame Edition was technically already teased back during Computex, though folks thought this showfloor piece was alluding to a whole new GPU generation at the time . Now, we know this special edition is actually current gen and will feature a GPU shroud encrusted with Swarovski crystals (via Techpowerup ). No price has yet been announced ahead of this exceptionally extra card's slated October 22 release date. With how much a standard RTX 5090 costs, odds are that those planning to scoop this shiny GPU will need very deep pockets indeed. For context, we've stopped including the RTX 5090 in the graphics card price watch , as our Dave notes the card is 'unavailable' from many reputable retailers. Our Jacob notes that the card can be found in places like Newegg's Marketplace for upwards of $9,000 . Those stones are far from the o…

title: Microsoft won't like this open source project to get Game Pass working on SteamOS and Linux, but I think it's pretty neat
summary: If it doesn't exist, build it yourself.
body: It wasn't long ago that Linux gaming was considered fairly niche—but given that Windows 11 is unpopular with many, it seems that not a day goes by without something regarding the switch to Linux hitting my newsfeed. Not to mention the continuing updates to Valve's Arch-based SteamOS. Now my attention has been drawn to the Xodus Nexus , an experimental open-source project that aims to allow Linux and SteamOS users to access PC Game Pass. This includes the ability to browse, install, and launch games via a very familiar interface, complete with cloud save support. That's for supported games only, of course, but the GitHub page has a big long list of them. From Gears of War: E-Day , to Minecraft for Windows, to Halo: Campaign Evolved , there sure are some big hitters that are already supported by the open-source platform. The readme describes the project as "An Xbox-inspired launcher built on Xodus , using our patched Nexus backend and Nexus runtime. Browse the store, install games you own or can access through a subscription, and play with one shared runtime." The whole system seems to be in an experimental test phase at the moment, and the controller navigation looks to be a work i…

title: Amnesia: The Dark Descent's co-founder explained the 'the dynamic of Steam' to Red Barrels after Outlast's sales slowed down
summary: "Basically, your sales curve becomes like a roller coaster."
body: Three of the most influential games from my childhood were Pokémon HeartGold, Amnesia: The Dark Descent , and Outlast . Knowing this, you could probably piece together the kind of person I have become—let's just say it explains a lot. So it brought a smile to my face when I learned that without one of these influential games, I wouldn't have had the other—no, Pokémon HeartGold has nothing to do with anything—it's actually Amnesia which helped bring Outlast to the world. Red Barrels, the Outlast devs, already discussed how difficult it was to pitch Outlast to publishers in an interview with GameSpot . But they also mentioned how Amnesia: The Dark Descent was something of a lodestar for the team. (Image credit: Red Barrels) Not only did the success of Amnesia reassure Red Barrels that there was in fact a market for the kind of game they were trying to make, but the fact that no one else had really tried to ride its coattails meant there was a space left wide open for them. Some of the Red Barrels devs even sat in on a conference talk where Frictional Games co-founder Thomas Grip revealed that Amnesia: The Dark Descent sold an impressive 400,000 copies in its first year. title: Moonlighter studio won't host a public playtest of its next game due to rampant AI-led cloning: 'We know we're not the only developers feeling this way'
summary: ReVamp will get a limited Discord playtest.
body: The studio behind the Moonlighter series has announced it will no longer host a public playtest for its forthcoming roguelike due to fears it will be "reverse-engineered, cloned and published". The move comes as a surge in rapidly vibe coded clones floods Steam, Roblox and mobile app stores in the aftermath of Claude Opus 5.5. "With launch still months away, sharing a build with tens of thousands of players feels like too big a risk," Digital Sun Games' marketing manager Israel Mallén told PC Gamer. The game under discussion is ReVamp , a "tower defensevania" roguelike due for release in March 2027. "We know we're not the only developers feeling this way, and the more this is talked about, the more likely platforms are to step in." In its public announcement Digital Sun Games was fairly blunt. "We've been concerned by recent news of games being reverse-engineered, cloned and published before the original is even out. With launch still months away, a large public build of ReVamp felt like too big a risk." Last week the studio behind Drunken Goddess Reflux canceled plans to roll out a public demo for Steam Next Fest due to similar fears. "We're concerned the demo's content could be …

title: Xbox biz guy deletes his X account less than 24 hours after saying game devs who don't embrace AI 'should not be in the business of being a business'
summary: Business strategy manager Brandon Stirrup said he was "happy to take the hit" for his stance on AI, then left social media.
body: Xbox senior business strategy manager Brandon Stirrup is tired of pussyfooting around about AI: In a thread on X his week, he said that he wants the world to know that Xbox uses it, that he thinks everyone should be using it, and that he believes so strongly in the cause that he's willing to "take the hit" for saying so. He has since deleted his X account. A source at Xbox tells PC Gamer that Stirrup opted to deactivate the account because of the volume of replies he was receiving. Stirrup kicked off his thread on October 18 with a simple message saying he'd "vibe coded a bad but improvable game" over two days, although he only "actively" worked on it for about three hours. "I’m telling you I tried it and it’s true…anyone can build a game." After saying that developers and studios who aren't incorporating AI into their strategies are "planning for a fake future," Stirrup went all in. "Look if I'm fired tomorrow it will be because I told you the truth that nobody wants you to know. You can make a game with a simple prompt and yes you can make custom, tailored games. Everything you want in a game is right there for the taking, for better or worse," he wrote. "I'm happy to take the h…

title: Two entire pallets of RTX 5090s have 'gone missing' from a Brazilian airport—$495,000 worth of unobtanium graphics cards now presumably at large
summary: Own up, which one of you was it?
body: Good news: I know of the existence of two entire pallets worth of RTX 5090 graphics cards—a rare thing in this day and age, as stock appears to have dwindled to virtually zero . Bad news, they've 'gone missing' from a Brazilian airport. Brazilian electronics distributor Oderço has published an Instagram post drawing attention to the missing Zotac GPUs, which supposedly arrived at Guarulhos International Airport in São Paulo, but then promptly vanished. "In our more than 38-year history, we have never encountered a situation like this—and we will not remain silent," says CEO Oderço Matos (via Tom's Hardware , machine translation). "Two pallets of Zotac RTX 5090 graphics cards have gone missing at Guarulhos International Airport. The merchandise is worth approximately R$2.5 million (at cost), and to date, we have received no answers." "We are seeking clarification and want to understand what happened," Matos continues. "How can a shipment of such value disappear from within an international airport without any explanation being provided to us?" The company has not provided the details of the shipment's arrival date or tracking numbers, but the Oderço Group CEO seems more than a litt…
